diagnosis.summary: The product-service Lambda handler is running far slower than its baseline, with all end-to-end latency percentiles elevated by roughly 100x to 173x. No 5xx errors are present on either service. Payment-service shows no handler degradation, though its request rate is elevated above baseline.
diagnosis.root_cause: Slow execution within the product-service Lambda handler is the most likely root cause. Payment-service Lambda duration is at or below baseline, making it an unlikely contributor to this incident.
evidence: product-service lambda_duration_ms_mean rose from 2.486 ms to 529.74 ms, an increase of roughly 213x, and lambda_duration_ms_p95 rose from 3.12 ms to 604.64 ms, roughly 194x.
product-service end-to-end latency rose across all measured percentiles: p50 from 4.09 ms to 708.27 ms (~173x), p95 from 6.56 ms to 718.75 ms (~110x), and p99 from 9.59 ms to 748.83 ms (~78x).
error_rate_5xx for both product-service and payment-service remains at 0, so no requests are currently returning server errors.
payment-service lambda_duration_ms_mean is 0.2554 ms, below its baseline of 0.5855 ms, and its p95 latency is 3.63 ms against a baseline of 4.51 ms, showing no handler slowdown.
payment-service request_rate is 2.1 rps against a baseline of 0.9433 rps, roughly 2.2x higher than normal.
recommended_actions: Check CloudWatch Logs at /aws/lambda/anomalypulse-product for slow code paths, exceptions, or any log lines showing unexpectedly long operations within the current incident window.

Review the CloudWatch Duration and Errors metrics for anomalypulse-product to determine whether any invocations are approaching or hitting the 10 s timeout, as those would not appear in error_rate_5xx or latency percentiles.

If a recent code, layer, or configuration change was deployed to anomalypulse-product, compare logs before and after to determine whether the slow path is in code that change touched before deciding to roll back.
After any remediation, recheck lambda_duration_ms_mean and p95_latency_ms for product-service to confirm the handler has returned to baseline.
Investigate why payment-service request_rate has risen to 2.1 rps from a baseline of 0.9433 rps to determine whether upstream call patterns have shifted.
